qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Owns prime central London office campuses (Broadgate, Regent's Place) and retail parks with significant planning barriers to entry. However, commercial real estate yields are structurally low (4-6%), producing a 10-year average ROIC of only 2.5-5.0%, far below the 12% hurdle. Commercial lease rents are negotiated tenant expenses, highly vulnerable to hybrid work office downsizing, corporate tenant restructurings, and cyclical interest rate shocks.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Prime London office campuses and retail parks face structural cap-rate realities, generating multi-year ROIC of only 2.5-5.0% against a 12% hurdle. Commercial rents lack true inflation pricing power, as tenants downsize office footprints amid hybrid working and higher borrowing costs depress property asset values.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year historical GAAP ROIC averages 2.5-5.0%, heavily depressed by periodic commercial property revaluation write-downs during UK interest rate increases. Total Accounting Return (TAR) targets of 8-10% rely on asset leverage rather than superior unlevered operational returns. Office portfolio faces persistent structural occupancy and lease renewal headwinds from corporate remote/hybrid working models.
